data.title: Samsung Stocks Close Up 2.6%; Goldman Defends Advanced-Memory Advantage
data.description:
Samsung Electronics, the memory and consumer-electronics giant (SSNLF), enters the U.S. morning with shares at ?215,500, up 2.62% at the October 16 Korean close, equivalent to 2:30 a.m. ET. According to Investing.com, Goldman Sachs argues that investors have overestimated how quickly Chinese competitors can catch Samsung in advanced DRAM and high-bandwidth memory. The investment question is straightforward: how much of that technology lead can Samsung turn into profit?

Samsung's October 8 guidance puts third-quarter revenue at approximately ?195 trillion and operating profit at ?107.4 trillion, compared with second-quarter results of ?171.5 trillion and ?89.49 trillion. That implies roughly 13.7% sales growth and 20% operating-profit growth sequentially. Those are consolidated figures, however. They do not reveal HBM profitability or establish how much of the improvement came from higher memory prices.

The financial acceleration is striking: guidance implies ?17.91 trillion of additional operating profit on ?23.5 trillion of additional revenue. That works out to a 76.2% incremental operating margin, a measure of the quarterly change rather than a sustainable group margin. The GF Score graphic shows 92/100, with strong growth, profitability and financial strength readings but a much weaker GF Value readinga reminder that business quality and valuation deserve separate scrutiny. The next segment breakdown needs to show where the earnings jump came from and how much staying power it has.

data.title: ExxonMobil Expects Q3 Earnings To Boost By $4.5 Bln From Refining Margins
data.description:
IRVING (dpa-AFX) - Friday, ExxonMobil Holdings Corp. (XOM) announced a preliminary statement that higher refining margins boosted its third-quarter earnings by an estimated $4.5 billion.

However, lower oil prices reduced earnings by $1.3 billion, while timing effects resulted in an estimated $2.5 billion impact.

The company explained that timing effects occur when open derivatives are valued using prices at the end of a reporting period, while the related physical shipments remain in inventory. These shipments are reflected in earnings only after the transactions are completed. ExxonMobil expects these effects to reverse in the coming quarters.

The filing also highlighted the impact of the Middle East situation, including losses on settled hedges that were not offset by physical shipments due to supply disruptions in the region.

XOM was trading at $177.55, up 1.60 percent on the NYSE.

data.title: Viatris, Opus granted FDA label expansion for Ryzumvi in presbyopia
data.description:
Opus Genetics on Friday announced that the U.S. FDA has granted a label expansion for Ryzumvi, an eye care solution it markets with Viatris , allowing its use in adults with presbyopia, an age-related condition characterized by loss of clear close-up vision.

The treatment, also known as phentolamine ophthalmic solution, was previously available in the U.S. for patients aged three years and older with pharmacologically induced mydriasis (dilated pupils).

The approval comes after the FDA accepted the company’s supplemental New Drug Application for Ryzumvi in presbyopia earlier this year, granting October 17 as the target action date.

The sNDA is backed by data from two pivotal Phase 3 trials, VEGA-2 and VEGA-3, which met their primary and all key secondary efficacy endpoints with a favorable safety profile for phentolamine ophthalmic solution.

Its approval triggers a milestone payment to Opus from Viatris . The companies reached a license and collaboration agreement in 2022 to market the PS treatment in the U.S. and several other overseas markets.

data.title: ExxonMobil Stock Is on Pace for a Record High. Preliminary Earnings Are Both Good and Bad. — Barrons.com
DHL Group Lifts Guidance After Positive Earnings, Strong Peak-Season Forecast
data.description:
By Andrea Figueras

DHL Group upgraded its outlook for 2026 on the back of positive momentum and prospects of a strong seasonal peak in the last quarter of the year.

The German logistics company said Friday that it now expects earnings before interest and taxes to surpass 7 billion euros, or $7.86 billion, compared with a prior forecast of more than 6.5 billion euros. The group intends to review its midterm earnings guidance in March.

"Business development in the third quarter showed a broad-based growth in demand and, overall, positive earnings momentum for the group, particularly in the DHL Express division," it said.

According to preliminary figures, the group made EBIT of roughly 1.71 billion euros for the quarter through September, up around 16% compared with the same period a year earlier. Group revenue jumped more than 12% on year to nearly 22.6 billion euros.

The company also upgraded its target for free cash flow excluding net mergers and acquisitions to more than 3.2 billion euros, up from approximately 3 billion euros previously.

Capital expenditure is now estimated at around 3.6 billion euros from a prior range between 3 billion euros and 3.3 billion euros.

DHL plans to publish its third-quarter report on Nov. 5.

data.title: UK's Thames Water reaches deal with key Class B creditors on recapitalisation
data.description:
Thames Water on Friday said it had reached an agreement with key Class B creditors on a proposed recapitalisation, securing support from holders of more than 60% of its junior Class B debt and advancing efforts to restructure Britain's biggest water utility.

The proposal would see about £1 billion ($1.33 billion) of Class B debt written off, with those creditors receiving a roughly 5.9% recovery through equity and other rights in the restructured company in return.

Thames Water said talks with the London & Valley Water consortium, Ofwat and other regulators on the proposed recapitalisation were ongoing, with no decision yet taken on whether to proceed with the consortium's proposal.

data.title: EU wheat falls as euro and Russian exports weigh
data.description:
Euronext wheat fell for a second session on Friday as a slide in Chicago, a bounce in the euro and a recovery in Russian exports weighed on prices after they hit a one-month high this week, traders said.

December milling wheat on Euronext settled 1% down at €244.75 ($274.71) a metric ton at the close.

The benchmark contract retreated from a one-month peak of €249.75 touched on Wednesday and again on Thursday.

A 17-month low for the euro against the dollar, a large import purchase by Algeria and ongoing attacks on Black Sea shipping had spurred gains in Euronext prices earlier in the week.

Illustrating unusual export demand generated by Black Sea disruption, a vessel is due to load 36,000 tons of French wheat for Oman later this month at the Atlantic port of La Pallice, LSEG data showed. (GRAIN/SHP/FR)

But a bounce in the euro since Thursday and signs of rising Russian exports through the Baltic Sea tempered export optimism in Western Europe.

Some Russian observers see potential for the country's wheat exports to rise to 3 million tons in October, extending a recovery from September, as traders expand use of rail logistics to supply Baltic ports.

"To have 3 million tons per month from Russia is not the usual 4.5-5 million post-harvest, but it's not zero and more than people expected," a futures trader said.

Chicago wheat dropped to a two-month low, with supply pressure from the US corn harvest also weighing.

In France, farmers had planted 15% of the expected soft wheat area for next year's harvest by October 12, lagging the average pace of the last five years, farm office FranceAgriMer said.

Traders are watching to see if rain forecast for the week ahead materializes and helps ease drought.

($1 = 0.8909 euros)

data.title: Nifty IT: Rs.3 lakh cr added in m-cap after best weekly gains in 18 years; Q2 earnings revive investor interest
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- Tech Mahindra, TCS, HCL Technologies, Infosys, and Wipro were among the large-cap IT stocks that ended the week with strong double-digit gains, powered by stronger-than-expected September-quarter performances and a weakening global AI trade that prompted investors to rotate back into the software sector.

Six of the 10 constituents of the Nifty IT index ended the week with gains of over 10%, with Tech Mahindra leading the pack after surging 18.7% as it closed higher in each of the last four trading sessions.

It was followed by Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), HCL Technologies, Infosys, Wipro, and LTM which ended the week with gains of 18.7%, 17.3%, 16.5%, 16.4%, and 12.1%, respectively.

Amid strong support from heavyweight stocks, the Nifty IT index finished the week with an 11.72% surge, marking its best weekly gain in 18 years. It reclaimed the 30,000 mark and also touched an eight-month high.

The recovery has also helped the stock recoup nearly half of its 2026 losses, after it had fallen 32%. The index's year-to-date decline now stands at 15.7%. Alongside, the recovery rally has boosted confidence on Dalal Street, helping the Nifty post its best weekly performance in six months.

The rally added nearly Rs.3 lakh crore to the combined market capitalization of the top 10 IT companies during the week.

The rally has provided a much-needed boost to a battered sector that had been plagued by fears of AI-driven disruption, concerns over interest rates, and sustained foreign institutional investor (FII) selling, dragging several constituents to multi-year lows.

However, the September-quarter results have offered investors some reassurance about the sector's near-term growth prospects, helping revive sentiment towards IT stocks.

Stronger-than-expected performances from major companies have also eased some concerns over slowing demand and the potential impact of artificial intelligence on traditional software services.

Tech Mahindra's second-quarter revenue came in above expectations, aided by robust deal wins, while Wipro also reported stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue, with signs that delayed large deals could support growth in the coming quarters.

HCL Tech's quarterly performance, stronger AI-related revenue, and healthy deal wins bolstered confidence in the sector's earnings outlook. TCS also delivered a healthy set of numbers for the second quarter.

The recent rally suggests that investors are reassessing valuations and returning to the sector after a prolonged sell-off. Whether the rebound can sustain its momentum will depend on the outlook for revenue growth, deal wins, client spending, and the extent to which IT companies can translate AI-related opportunities into meaningful business growth.

But with LED, QLED, and OLED TVs available across different brands and prices, knowing which one to choose can be confusing.

LED TVs are generally more affordable and suitable for everyday entertainment, while QLED models offer brighter, more vibrant colours that work well in sunlit living rooms. OLED TVs, on the other hand, deliver deeper blacks and sharper contrast, making dark movie scenes look more realistic. Understanding these differences can help you choose a TV that suits your viewing habits, room lighting, and budget.

An OLED TV uses self-emitting pixels instead of a separate backlight. Each pixel can switch off independently, producing true blacks and precise contrast.

This makes OLED particularly appealing for films with dark scenes, gaming, and viewing from different seating positions.

data.title: SAP Stocks Slip Although TD Cowen Lifts Target 22%
data.description:
SAP, the enterprise-software provider , heads toward its next earnings report with TD Cowen's price target lifted nearly 22% to $250, while its U.S. shares traded at $224.33, down 0.30%, at 10:59 a.m. ET on October 16. According to The Fly, analyst Derrick Wood retained his Buy rating and raised the target from $205. That gives investors a higher benchmark. SAP still has to deliver the growth to support it.

The cloud business is doing the heavy lifting. SAP's July results showed second-quarter cloud revenue of 6.281 billion, up from 5.130 billion a year earlier. Software-support revenue moved the other way, falling to 2.439 billion from 2.642 billion. Current cloud backlog reached 22.929 billion, giving the company revenue visibility rather than revenue already booked. The financial snapshot shows a GF Score of 90/100 alongside a P/E of 28.2, putting a strong overall score next to a valuation that still demands execution.

Here is the hurdle: the 203 million decline in support revenue offset 17.6% of the 1.151 billion cloud-revenue increase, before other businesses entered the calculation. Moving customers to the cloud creates growth while shrinking an older income stream. My test for the next report is whether SAP can turn that migration into faster total revenue growth while protecting cloud profitability. Second-quarter IFRS cloud gross margin stood at 74.3%. A higher target strengthens the bullish case; stronger growth and steadier margins would give it financial backing.

data.title: US regional banks join bigger peers in signaling resilient economy as lending holds firm
data.description:
By Pritam Biswas, Arasu Kannagi Basil and Prakhar Srivastava

A clutch of US regional banks reported strong third-quarter earnings this week, powered by robust loan demand from businesses, adding to signs that the economy remained resilient despite rising borrowing costs.

Earlier in the week, the biggest US banks such as JPMorgan Chase , Bank of America , Wells Fargo and Citigroup also reported higher loan balances, even as weakness in the capital markets hit their investment banking revenue.

People have accepted global uncertainty as the new normal and are pushing forward with operations, PNC Financial CEO William Demchak said.

"The clouds are as dark as they ever were, but the economy's still strong. People are investing into it," Demchak added.

PNC led the regional banks' loan growth at 14.2% in the third quarter, followed by U.S. Bancorp at 8%, M&T Bank at 5.5% and Citizens Financial at 5.29%.

The robust borrowing activity defied rising expectations that still-high inflation fueled by the Iran war and the Federal Reserve's September interest rate hike could chill corporate capital expenditures and dampen borrowing appetite.

Top regional banking executives said loan pipelines remained strong and they had not seen any slowdown yet in demand.

Citizens Financial said loan demand actually started to pick up in the last couple of weeks as the bank entered the fourth quarter.

AI CATALYST?

Banking executives said they were looking to understand how much of the loan growth was linked to the massive AI-related spending when pressed by analysts during post-earnings sessions.

"This whole AI ecosystem build-out is kind of full-on. It's a very strong dynamic, and that kind of cascades into a lot of the supply ecosystem," Citizens Financial CEO Bruce Van Saun said.

"Even with higher rates, the kind of desire to get the compute power in place, the players aren't really batting an eyelash," he added.

PNC, which does not have a large data-center finance business, said there is an impact from the AI spending boom on tangential sectors like heavy equipment, transportation and energy.

"If the capex broadly slows down related to AI, do we think, even though we don't lend directly to that, it would slower loan growth? Yes, I do," PNC's Demchak said.

Some regional banks downplayed the AI dependency and emphasized broad-based commercial and industrial loan growth.

U.S. Bancorp CFO John Stern said loan growth was robust even outside AI-adjacent sectors, highlighting areas like retail, food and beverage, and insurance.

The board of directors of MGE Energy, Inc. (), today declared the regular quarterly dividend of $0.5083 per share on the outstanding shares of the company's common stock, payable December 15, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business December 1, 2026.

MGE Energy has increased its dividend annually for the past 51 years and has paid cash dividends for more than 115 years.

About MGE Energy

MGE Energy is a public utility holding company. Its principal subsidiary, Madison Gas and Electric, generates and distributes electricity to 170,000 customers in Dane County, Wis., and purchases and distributes natural gas to 180,000 customers in seven south-central and western Wisconsin counties. MGE's roots in the Madison area date back more than 150 years.

data.title: Charles Schwab says Bitcoin still has strong fundamentals for the future
data.description:
Charles Schwab's crypto research team says the asset still has strong fundamentals for the future, and it expects regulatory progress to help the broader market.

Analyst Adam Lynch made the bullish case on October 15, 2026. He pointed to nearly $60 billion in ETF inflows since early 2024 as evidence that demand runs deeper than a passing trend.

"Bitcoin is strong. It's powerful... still has strong fundamentals for the future," Lynch said.

Jim Ferraioli, Schwab's Head of Crypto Research, noted that Bitcoin's volatility now sits at about 40, down from a previous range of 50 to 60. He also put Bitcoin's market cap at approximately $1.6 trillion and said the tokenization of real-world assets has reached around $50 billion.

On regulation, the team cited progress in the US, including clarity on Bitcoin and Ether as digital commodities.

Schwab completed the full retail rollout of Schwab Crypto around October 16, 2026. Eligible clients can now trade Bitcoin and Ether directly inside their Schwab accounts. Each trade carries a fee of 0.75%. Schwab plans to add more tokens to the platform by the end of the year.

The service runs through Schwab's Premier Bank, with Paxos providing sub-custody support and handling execution.

CEO Rick Wurster has described crypto trading as a new source of revenue for the firm. Schwab's clients hold approximately 20% of the assets in spot crypto ETFs, within Schwab's $13 trillion in managed assets.

Schwab's research suggests modest allocations to crypto within diversified portfolios.

The 0.75% fee will be one point of comparison for cost-conscious traders. Watch, too, whether Schwab follows through on its plan to add more tokens by year-end.

data.title: Proofpoint CEO: Varonis Deal is Play for Data Security Market — Market Talk
data.description: Proofpoint's roughly $6.3 billion acquisition of cybersecurity firm Varonis Systems is a play to dominate the market for data security services, Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan says on CNBC. "Data has become the next frontier of protection for cybersecurity," Dhawan says, adding that enterprises need data security in order to deploy AI safely. "Proofpoint and Varonis together become the largest cybersecurity player solving data security," he says. "None of the other providers were designed and built for protecting data, and Proofpoint and Varonis is." Varonis shares trade up 2.9% at $48.69 (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)
